pairs: Igitur cum Tobias putaret orationem suam exaudiri ut mori potuisset,
Therefore, when Tobit considered that his prayer was heard, so that he might be able to die,
vocavit ad se Tobiam filium suum,
he called his son Tobias to him.
dixitque ei: Audi,
And he said to him:
fili mi,
“My son,
verba oris mei,
hear the words of my mouth,
et ea in corde tuo quasi fundamentum construe.
and set them, like a foundation, in your heart.
Cum acceperit Deus animam meam,
When God will receive my soul,
corpus meum sepeli:
bury my body.
et honorem habebis matri tuæ omnibus diebus vitæ ejus:
And you shall honor your mother, all the days of her life.
memor enim esse debes, quæ et quanta pericula passa sit propter te in utero suo.
For you are obliged to be mindful of what great perils she suffered because of you in her womb.
Cum autem et ipsa compleverit tempus vitæ suæ,
But when she too will have completed the time of her life,
sepelias eam circa me.
bury her near me.
Omnibus autem diebus vitæ tuæ in mente habeto Deum:
Yet, for all the days of your life, have God in your mind.
et cave ne aliquando peccato consentias,
And be careful that you never consent to sin,
et prætermittas præcepta Domini Dei nostri.
nor overlook the precepts of the Lord our God.
Ex substantia tua fac eleemosynam,
Give alms from your substance,
et noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere:
and do not turn away your face from any pauper.
ita enim fiet ut nec a te avertatur facies Domini.
For so it shall be that neither will the face of the Lord be turned away from you.
Quomodo potueris,
In whatever way that you are able,
ita esto misericors.
so shall you be merciful.
Si multum tibi fuerit,
If you have much,
abundanter tribue:
distribute abundantly.
si exiguum tibi fuerit,
If you have little,
etiam exiguum libenter impertiri stude.
nevertheless strive to bestow a little freely.
Præmium enim bonum tibi thesaurizas in die necessitatis:
For you store up for yourself a good reward for the day of necessity.
quoniam eleemosyna ab omni peccato et a morte liberat,
For almsgiving liberates from every sin and from death,
et non patietur animam ire in tenebras.
and it will not suffer the soul to go into darkness.
Fiducia magna erit coram summo Deo,
Almsgiving will be a great act of faith before the most high God,
eleemosyna omnibus facientibus eam.
for all those who practice it.
Attende tibi, fili mi,
Take care to keep yourself,
ab omni fornicatione,
my son, from all fornication,
et præter uxorem tuam numquam patiaris crimen scire.
and, except for your wife, never permit yourself to know such an offense.
Superbiam numquam in tuo sensu
Never permit arrogance to rule in your mind or in your words.
aut in tuo verbo dominari permittas:
For in it,
in ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio.
all perdition had its beginning.
Quicumque tibi aliquid operatus fuerit,
And whoever has done any kind of work for you,
statim ei mercedem restitue,
immediately pay him his wages,
et merces mercenarii tui apud te omnino non remaneat.
and do not let the wages of your hired hand remain with you at all.
Quod ab alio oderis fieri tibi,
Whatever you would hate to have done to you by another,
vide ne tu aliquando alteri facias.
see that you never do so to another.
Panem tuum cum esurientibus et egenis comede,
Eat your bread with the hungry and the needy,
et de vestimentis tuis nudos tege.
and cover the naked with your own garments.
Panem tuum et vinum tuum super sepulturam justi constitue,
Set out your bread and your wine at the burial of a just man,
et noli ex eo manducare et bibere cum peccatoribus.
and do not eat and drink from it with sinners.
Consilium semper a sapiente perquire.
Always seek the counsel of a wise man.
Omni tempore benedic Deum:
Bless God at all times.
et pete ab eo ut vias tuas dirigat,
And petition him that he direct your ways
et omnia consilia tua in ipso permaneant.
and that all your counsels may remain in him.
Indico etiam tibi,
And now, I reveal to you,
fili mi,
my son,
dedisse me decem talenta argenti,
that I lent ten talents of silver,
dum adhuc infantulus esses,
while you were still a young child,
Gabelo,
to Gabael,
in Rages civitate Medorum,
in Rages, a city of the Medes,
et chirographum ejus apud me habeo:
and I have his written agreement with me.
et ideo perquire quomodo ad eum pervenias,
And so,
et recipias ab eo supra memoratum pondus argenti,
inquire how you may travel to him and receive from him the aforementioned weight of silver,
et restituas ei chirographum suum.
and return to him the written agreement.
Noli timere,
Do not be afraid,
fili mi:
my son.
pauperem quidem vitam gerimus,
We do indeed lead a poor life,
sed multa bona habebimus si timuerimus Deum,
but we will have many good things: if we fear God,
et recesserimus ab omni peccato,
and withdraw from all sin,
et fecerimus bene.
and do what is good.”
